en: Regarding the *Sūmaṭī-sūtra*, the *Kāiyuán lù* states it is the *Miaohuì tóngnǚ jīng*. It was translated later by Fǎliúzhì;
the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang, by imperial decree, translated it as follows:
Thus have I heard: At one time the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak in the city of Rājagṛha, together with...
There were one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus and ten thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in the assembly.

At that time, there was the daughter of an elder in the city of Rājagṛha named Prajñākūṭā, who was eight years of age. Her features were upright, her complexion was beautiful, and she was endowed with all the auspicious marks; those who saw her rejoiced. She had previously drawn near to and made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas of the past, planting various roots of goodness.
Then that woman went to the place where the Tathāgata was, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, knelt with palms joined, and spoke these verses:
“The Unsurpassed Perfectly Awakened One, Is the Great Bright Lamp for the World.”
"The conduct of a bodhisattva—may you graciously permit me to inquire about it.
The Buddha told Miaohui:
"Now ask whatever you wish; I shall explain it for you so that your web of doubts may be severed."
At that time, Prajñāvatī immediately asked the Buddha in verse:
"How may one obtain a handsome body, And a life of great wealth and noble status?"
Furthermore, by what causes and conditions are one's retinue difficult to disperse?
How does one perceive one's own body as being born through transformation upon a thousand-petaled lotus flower,
personally attending all the World-Honored Ones face-to-face?
How can one realize and attain the supreme, sovereign supernormal powers,
so as to travel everywhere to immeasurable lands to pay homage to all Buddhas?
How can one become free from enmity, such that whatever one says is trusted and accepted by others?
How does one purify the obstructions to the Dharma and forever leave behind all demonic activities?
How, at the time of death, may one behold the Buddhas,
hear them preach the pure Dharma, and not undergo further suffering?
"O Great Compassionate, Unsurpassed Honored One!
I pray that you will speak for me.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the girl Miaohui, saying:
“Excellent, excellent! You have skillfully asked about this profound and subtle meaning.
Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon it well; I shall explain it for you.”
The Girl Prajñā replied:
“So be it, World-Honored One!
I am eager and desirous to hear.”
The Buddha said,
“妙慧 (Wondrous Wisdom)!
A bodhisattva who accomplishes four dharmas receives a handsome body.”
What are the four?
First, not giving rise to anger toward evil associates; second, abiding in great loving-kindness; third, deeply delighting in the true Dharma; and fourth, fashioning images of the Buddha.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:

“Do not allow anger to increase, for it destroys the roots of goodness; By cultivating a mind of loving-kindness, delighting in the Dharma, and fashioning images of the Buddha, One shall obtain a body adorned with the primary and secondary marks, Which all sentient beings will always joyfully behold.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
A bodhisattva who accomplishes four dharmas attains a body of wealth and nobility.
What are these four?
First, giving at the appropriate time; second, being free from a mind of contempt or arrogance; third, bestowing with joy; fourth, not seeking a karmic reward.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
“Giving at the proper time, without contempt, Bestowing with joy and without expectation—
If one can constantly and diligently cultivate such karma, One shall obtain great wealth and status in whatever birth one takes.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
A bodhisattva who accomplishes four dharmas will obtain an indestructible retinue.
What are these four?

First, they are skillfully able to abandon and relinquish divisive speech; second, they cause sentient beings with wrong views to abide in right view; third, when the True Dharma is about to perish, they protect it so that it may endure for a long time; fourth, they teach all beings to aspire toward the Bodhi of the Buddha.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
"Abandoning divisive speech and false views, Being able to protect and uphold the True Dharma as it nears extinction,
And establishing sentient beings in great Bodhi— Such a one shall attain an indestructible retinue."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva accomplishes four dharmas, they shall receive birth by transformation before the Buddha and dwell upon a lotus seat.
What are these four?

First, to take various flowers, fruits, and fine powdered incense and scatter them over the Tathāgata and all his stūpas and shrines; second, never to falsely inflict harm upon others; third, to fashion images of the Tathāgata and place them within lotuses; and fourth, to give rise to profound pure faith in the Bodhi of the Buddha.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"Scattering flowers before the Buddha and the caityas, refraining from harming others and fashioning images,
and having deep faith and understanding in Great Bodhi— one shall attain birth before the Buddha upon a lotus flower."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
A bodhisattva who accomplishes four dharmas travels from one buddha-field to another.
What are these four?

First, seeing others cultivate goodness, one does not create obstacles or cause them distress; second, when others preach the Dharma, one never hinders or obstructs them; third, one offers lamps as an offering to the stūpas of the Tathāgata; fourth, one constantly and diligently practices all meditative concentrations.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"Seeing people practicing virtue and preaching the True Dharma, One does not give rise to slander or create obstacles;
Offering lamps at the stūpas and shrines of the Tathāgata, One cultivates the various dhyānas and wanders through the Buddha-fields."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
A bodhisattva who accomplishes four dharmas dwells in the world without enmity.
What are these four?

First, to associate with virtuous friends with a mind free from deceit; second, to have no heart of envy toward the superior dharmas of others; third, to always feel joy in one's heart when others obtain renown; and fourth, to have no mind of disparagement or contempt toward the practices of bodhisattvas.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
"One does not associate with virtuous friends through flattery; one harbors no envy toward the superior Dharma of others;
one always rejoices when others attain renown; and by not slandering Bodhisattvas, one becomes free from enmity."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva accomplishes four dharmas, people believe what they say.
What are these four?

First, one’s speech and practice must always be in accord; second, one does not conceal any evils before virtuous friends; third, one does not seek out faults in the Dharma one hears; fourth, one does not give rise to malice toward those who preach the Dharma.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
“Speech and practice are always in accord; One does not conceal one’s own faults from virtuous friends;
Hearing the sutras, one seeks not the faults of persons or dharmas; Everything that is spoken is received with faith.”
"Furthermore, Wondrous Wisdom!
If a bodhisattva accomplishes four dharmas, they can leave behind the obstacles to the Dharma and swiftly attain purity.
What are these four?

First, to encompass the threefold restraint through profound intention; second, not to give rise to slander upon hearing extremely profound sutras; third, to give rise to the mind of omniscience upon seeing bodhisattvas who have newly resolved their minds; and fourth, to maintain great and impartial compassion toward all sentient beings.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"By means of profound aspiration, one upholds the discipline; Hearing the most profound sutras, one is able to believe and understand them.
Honoring those who have first resolved their minds as if they were Buddhas, With a heart of universal compassion, all obstacles are eliminated."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
A bodhisattva who accomplishes four dharmas is able to remain free from all māras.
What are these four?

First, thoroughly understanding the equality of the nature of phenomena; second, initiating diligence; third, constantly and assiduously recollecting the Buddha; and fourth, dedicating all roots of goodness.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
“Those who can know the equality of all phenomena, who constantly arouse diligence, mindfulness of the Tathāgata,
and dedicate all roots of goodness— no demons shall be able to find an opportunity against them.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva accomplishes four dharmas, at the time of death all Buddhas will appear before them.
What are these four?

First, to fulfill the requests of others when they seek something; second, to develop profound faith and understanding in all wholesome dharmas; third, to bestow ornaments upon bodhisattvas; and fourth, to diligently cultivate offerings to the Triple Gem.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
"To satisfy the needs of others who seek help, To have faith and understanding in the profound Dharma,
To relinquish ornaments and diligently make offerings To the Triple Gem, the field of merit— At the moment of death, the Buddha will appear before one."
At that time, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, the maiden Prajñāvatī addressed him, saying:
"World-Honored One!
As for the various practices of a bodhisattva as taught by the Buddha, I shall respectfully practice them."
World-Honored One!
If I were to omit even a single one of these forty practices and fail to cultivate it, I would be contravening the Buddha's teaching and deceiving the Tathāgata.
At that time, the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana said to Prajñākūṭa:
"The conduct of a bodhisattva is extremely difficult to practice.
Now that you have made such a sublime and great vow, do you possess mastery over this vow?"
At that time, Prajñāvatī addressed him, saying:
"Venerable One!
If my great vow is true and not false, and if it can cause all practices to reach fulfillment, may this trichiliocosm tremble in six ways."
At that time, Prajñāvatī addressed Maudgalyāyana once more:

“By virtue of these words of truth of mine, may I attain Buddhahood in a future age—just like the Tathāgata Śākyamuni today—and in my land, may there be no demonic activities, nor any evil realms, nor even the name of ‘woman.’”
“If these words of mine are not false, may the bodies of this great assembly all become golden.
As soon as he had spoken these words, the entire assembly became golden.
At that time, the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and said:
“World-Honored One!
I now first pay homage to the bodhisattvas who have newly resolved their minds for awakening, as well as to the assembly of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
At that time, Mañjuśrī, the Dharma Prince, addressed Wondrous Wisdom, saying:
“In what dharma do you abide to make such a sincere vow?
Mañjuśrī, Mahāmati replied: “Mañjuśrī!...”
This is not what was asked.
Why? Because within the dharma-realm there is no place of abiding.
He asked again:
"What is called 'bodhi'? He replied:
“The non-conceptual dharma is called bodhi.
He asked again:
“What is meant by ‘bodhisattva’?”
He replied:
"All dharmas are equal to the characteristic of empty space; this is called a bodhisattva.
He asked again:
"What is called the practice of bodhi? He replied:
"The practice of bodhi is like the practice of a mirage or an echo."
He asked again:
"Based on what underlying intention (saṃdhāya) was this said? He replied:
“I do not perceive even the slightest dharma herein that is either secret or not secret.
He asked again, “If this is so,
then all ordinary beings should be enlightenment itself.”
He replied:
"Do you think that awakening (bodhi) is something different from ordinary beings?
Do not hold such a view."
"Why is this? Because all these share the same characteristic of the single Dharma-realm; they are neither grasped nor abandoned, for there is neither formation nor destruction.
He asked again:
“How many are there who can understand this meaning?
He replied,
“As many as the measure of illusory minds and mental factors, so many illusory sentient beings can understand this meaning.”
Mañjuśrī said: “Since illusions and transformations are fundamentally non-existent, how could there be such mental states and mental factors?
He replied:
“The Dharma-realm is likewise: it is neither existent nor non-existent;
even the Tathāgata is also thus.
At that time, Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This Subhūti is truly rare, being able to accomplish such a dharma-patience.
The Buddha said:
"It is so, it is so; it is exactly as you have said.

However, this young girl has already resolved her mind upon supreme enlightenment in the past, while I only set out for unsurpassed enlightenment thirty kalpas ago. She has also caused you to abide in the patience of non-arising."
At that time, Mañjuśrī rose from his seat, paid homage to her, and said to Prajñāśrī:
"In the past, during immeasurable kalpas ago, I have already made offerings to you; I did not expect that I would now once again have the opportunity to draw near to you."
Sudhī replied: "Mañjuśrī!
You should not now give rise to such conceptual discrimination."
"Why is this? Because one attains the patience of non-arising through non-discrimination.
He asked again:
“Sudhīmatī! Have you still not yet transformed your female body?
Sudhīmatī replied:
"The characteristics of a woman are utterly unfindable;
what, then, could be transformed? "Mañjuśrī!
I shall eliminate your doubts for you."

"By virtue of this true speech of mine, when I attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in a future age, may all the bhikṣus within my Dharma who hear the call 'Come, well-come' and go forth into the path have bodies that are entirely golden. May all sentient beings in my land possess clothing, utensils, and requisites like those of the Sixth Heaven; may food and drink be abundant and arrive according to their thoughts. May there be no demonic activities or evil realms, nor even the name of 'woman. May there be groves of the seven treasures draped with jeweled nets and covered with canopies of seven-treasure lotuses—just as in the pure land established by Mañjuśrī, its adornments and decorations shall be identical and without difference."

"If these words of mine are not false, may the bodies of this great assembly all become golden in color, and may my female body be transformed into that of a male, like a thirty-year-old bhikṣu who knows the Dharma."

When these words were spoken, this entire great assembly all became golden in color; the Bodhisattva Wondrous Wisdom transformed her female form into a male one, appearing like a thirty-year-old bhikṣu who knows the Dharma.
At that time, the hosts of earth-dwelling devas praised one another, saying:
"How great! How great!
When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Subhūti attains enlightenment in a future age, his adornment of the Buddha-field will possess such merit."
At that time, the Buddha addressed Mañjuśrī:
"In a future age, this Bodhisattva Prajñāvatī shall attain equal and right enlightenment, appearing in the world under the name Tathāgata Viśiṣṭaguṇaratnagarbha."

When the Buddha spoke this sutra, thirty koṭis of sentient beings became established in non-retrogression regarding anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; eighty koṭis of sentient beings were distanced from dust and free from defilement, attaining the pure Dharma-eye; and eight thousand sentient beings all attained realization through wisdom.

Five thousand bhikṣus who had set out upon the bodhisattva vehicle and whose minds were inclined toward regression, because they witnessed the excellence of the Bodhisattva Prajñā’s noble intention, roots of goodness, and majestic virtue, each removed the upper robe they were wearing and offered it to the Tathāgata.
Having given such gifts, they made this solemn vow:
"By these roots of goodness, we resolutely aspire to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

Because those sons of good family dedicated these roots of goodness toward unexcelled bodhi, they transcended the suffering of birth and death for ninety kalpas and became non-retrogressive from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, the World-Honored One immediately bestowed this prediction upon them:

"In a future age, after a thousand kalpas have passed, during the Stainless Radiance Kalpa, in the world-system of Mirage within the Buddha-field of Hard to Endure, you shall all successively attain Buddhahood within a single kalpa. You shall all share the same name, Venerable Eloquence Ornament Tathāgata, appearing in the world."
“Mañjuśrī! This Dharma gate possesses great majestic power; it can bring about great benefit for both bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and those of the śrāvaka vehicle.”

Mañjuśrī! Suppose there are sons or daughters of good family who, seeking bodhi, practice the six pāramitās for a full thousand kalpas without skillful means; yet if another person were to write out and recite this sūtra even once during the period of half a month, the mass of merit obtained by the latter would surpass the former’s virtue by a factor of a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand koṭis, or even beyond what can be reached by calculation or analogy.

"Therefore, Mañjuśrī, this subtle and wondrous Dharma-gate is the very foundation of the sūtras for all bodhisattvas. I now entrust it to you; in future ages, you should receive, uphold, read, recite, and explain it to others."
For example, when a Wheel-Turning Sage King appears in the world, all seven treasures manifest before him;
yet after the king passes away, the treasures all vanish.
If such a subtle and wondrous Dharma-gate circulates in the world, then the light of the Dharma—such as the seven factors of enlightenment and other qualities of all Tathāgatas—will not perish;
if it does not circulate, the True Dharma shall surely perish.
"Therefore, Mañjuśrī! If good sons and good daughters seek awakening, they should arouse diligence to copy this sutra, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, and explain it to others."
"This is my teaching; do not harbor regretful thoughts in future lives.

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, the Bodhisattva Wondrous Wisdom, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, and the great assembly—including devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others—having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced, and they faithfully accepted and practiced it.
The Sūtra of Sumati (Sūmaṭī)
